market_index_2026:
Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index (MUVVI) in 2026, all figures from Cox Automotive, CollisionWeek and CMD+RVL snippets:
- March 2026: 215.3, +6.2% YoY. This was the 2026 peak, driven by the tax-refund season.
- July 2026: 210.0, -1.4% MoM, +1.3% YoY, about 2.5% below the March high. Segment YoY: EVs +10.5%, compact cars +4.1%, midsize cars -1.4%, SUVs -1.7%, pickups -2.3%.
- August 2026: 208.2, -0.9% MoM, +0.4% YoY ('weakest pace since December 2025'). Non-adjusted prices +0.2% YoY. Cox: 'resilience in EV and compact-car prices was offset by continued declines in pickups and SUVs.'
- Mid-September 2026 (first 15 days): 206.2, -1.0% vs August, -0.4% vs September 2025. This is the first negative YoY reading of 2026. Non-adjusted prices -1.1% MoM and -1.1% YoY. 'Compact cars and electric vehicles were the only major segments still holding above year-ago values.' The full September data is due Oct 7, 2026.

Forecasts:
- Cox (January 2026 forecast, via CNBC): the Manheim index would end 2026 2% above December 2025.
- Cox also reports retail used prices 'up about 3% year-over-year, nearly touching $30,500 on average' as of mid-2026. Q2 2026 headline: 'MUVVI normalizes in Q2 after strong start; retail used prices climb higher.'
- J.D. Power: average used-vehicle price in 2026 is $30,166 (+$860 YoY). Used supply is expected to rise in coming years as post-pandemic production recovers.
- I found no explicit numeric Cox or J.D. Power forecast for 2027 used prices.

ESTIMATE (my inference, not a published forecast): wholesale roughly flat to -3% from late 2026 to Aug 2027. Compact cars and hybrids hold better; SUVs and luxury SUVs soften more. There will be a spring 2027 tax-season bump and then a summer decline.

seasonality_and_madison_august:
Seasonality in the 2026 Manheim data:
- Wholesale values peaked in March 2026 (215.3, tax-refund season).
- They then declined month after month: July -1.4% MoM, August -0.9%, first half of September -1.0%.
- So the October 2026 purchase falls near the fall low point. The August 2027 sale falls after the spring peak and usually about 2-3% below it (based on the 2026 pattern: July was about 2.5% below March).

Implication (ESTIMATE):
- Buying in October to November is favorable.
- Selling in August is not the best month in general, since spring (March to April) is best. However, local private-party demand in August may offset this.

Madison August student demand: NOT VERIFIED. The shared WebSearch pool ran out (the harness reported 200 of 200 calls used) before I could search for Madison or UW student-demand evidence, August 15 lease turnover, or Craigslist and Facebook price behavior. Treat 'August student demand raises cheap-car prices in Madison' as an unverified hypothesis.

Practical note (ESTIMATE): listing privately in late July to early August, before the semester starts, targets arriving students and families. That is the main lever for beating instant-offer prices.

Buying private party (or deeply below the CarGurus average) and selling private party is the main way to reduce total cost.

summary:
This is based on 37 successful WebSearch calls. After that, the shared 200-call pool was reported exhausted (the sibling agent used the rest), so I stopped.

Market:
- The Manheim wholesale index peaked at 215.3 in March 2026 (+6.2% YoY).
- It then slid to 210.0 in July (+1.3% YoY), 208.2 in August (+0.4% YoY) and 206.2 in mid-September (-0.4% YoY, the first negative reading of 2026).
- Compact cars and EVs are the only segments above year-ago levels. SUVs, pickups and midsize cars are declining.
- Gas is elevated (the search summary gave a range of about $4.00-$5.75 as of September 28, 2026, and a record diesel price of $6.53 on September 22). Newer used hybrids are surging: iSeeCars reports 1-5-year-old hybrid share +41.8% in Q1 2026, used hybrid sales +34% YTD, and a record average list price of $38,800. The 2013 Prius cohort, however, is only +1.7% YoY on CarGurus.
- Cox's January 2026 forecast called for the index to end 2026 2% above December 2025. J.D. Power puts the 2026 average used price at $30,166 (+$860). I found no numeric 2027 forecast.

Model cohort trends (CarGurus, same model year, asking average and YoY change, September 2026):
- 2012 ES: $11,602, +3.3% (Chicago $12,212, +5.2%)
- 2014 ES: $15,522, +6.7%
- 2011 RX 350 AWD: $11,648, +0.1%
- IS 250 AWD: $12,081, +10.9% in Virginia but -4.8% in Oregon
- 2008 GX 470: $17,789 average (range $8,909-$30,796)
- 2013 Camry: $10,888, +1.5%
- 2015 Corolla: $11,837, flat
- 2013 Prius: $9,485, +1.7%
- 2012 RAV4 4WD: $10,516-$10,686, -0.7% to +1.3%
- 2011 Highlander: $10,943, +0.9%
- LR4 (all years): $13,399, -3.8% to -12.8% regionally
- 2011 Range Rover Sport: about $9,043, -2.3% to -5.4%
- 2013 Evoque: $10.3-11.3k, -4.2% to +2.4%

Edmunds private-party values assume about 12k mi/yr and are much lower than the asking averages, for example 2011 RX $7,526, 2011 ES $8,153, 2015 Corolla $6,664 and 2012 LR4 $8,118. Trade-in runs about 72-80% of private party for Toyota and Lexus, and about 55-60% for the LR4 and the 2011 ES.

Concrete listings: I verified few. There is one Chicago 2010 RX 350 AWD at 121,682 miles for $13,990, a Wisconsin RX 350 floor of $9,399, and Mad Motors Madison Lexus inventory starting at $5,495. A TrueCar snippet showing a 2011 ES at 55k miles for $24,998 is unreliable.

Resale ESTIMATES for Aug 2027 (my inference, not observed):
- Corolla, Prius and 2013-14 ES: 0% to -5%
- Camry, RAV4, Highlander, RX and 2010-12 ES: -3% to -8%
- IS 250: -5% to -10%
- Land Rover models: -8% to -15%, plus high repair risk

Still not gathered: actual CarMax, Carvana or KBB ICO amounts; Madison August student-demand evidence; and a 2027 Cox or J.D. Power numeric outlook.

market_notes:
OBSERVED ASKING PRICES (from search-result summaries only; post dates were almost never visible)
- Lexus RX 350: 2013 AWD at $11,787-$11,889 (Wausau, CL); 2010 at $10,750 (Madison CL); dealer 2013 AWD with 98,690 mi at Stark on the Beltline, price hidden; over budget: 2017 with 96k at about $22.4k-22.9k (Madison dealer) and 2010 RX 450h with 49k at $17,900 (Stoughton, "No Dealer Fee's"). One search summary put the 2013 RX at about $10,150-10,950 trade-in and $12,900-14,350 private party (the source KBB/Edmunds page was not shown). Edmunds' appraisal page title gives $6,113-$14,824 for a 2013 RX 350. CarGurus counts 475 used RX near Madison, $4,091-$60,150, average about $30k.
- Lexus ES: 2011 ES 350 $6,200 (West Allis); 2009 ES 350 with 157k $7,000 (Milwaukee FB); 2008 ES 350 $10,300 (Rockford); 2013 ES 350 $14,995-15,500 (West Madison, over budget); a suspicious 2018 ES 350 at $10,900. ES 300/330 from 2002-2006 run $2,800-$5,500.
- Other Lexus: 2006 GX 470 with 213k $5,600 (Edgerton); LX 470 $9,500; LS 460 AWD $12,300; 2004 LS 430 $7,500; RX 330 $4,500-7,900; IS 250 $4,250; RX 400h $4,250. Over budget: 2012 GX 460 $18,700 (Wisconsin Dells).
- Toyota: Camry private sales run $1,500 (2007, 180k) up to $13,500 (2011 V6, 50k). Madison dealer Camrys: 2012 XLE with 121k $10,311, 2016 LE Hybrid $10,979, 2012 LE with 50k $15,987, 2018 SE with 89k $16,994. RAV4 private: 2012 Limited with 161k $4,850; 2002-2004 at $3,200-4,750.
- Land Rover private in the Madison area: 2011 RR Sport HSE with 130k $8,999-9,999; 2005 RR HSE $3,200-3,500; 2007 RR Sport $1,000-2,000. These are cheap to buy and expensive to own; not recommended for the TCO goal.
- Cars.com summary: "2 great deals out of 30 listings starting at $7,872" for Lexus near Arlington, WI.

SHORTLIST FOR LOWEST TCO FROM THESE CHANNELS (all estimates)
1) 2013 RX 350 AWD at about $11.8k (Wausau): best Lexus AWD value if miles are under about 130k and the title is clean. Purchase plus 5.5% tax is about $12.45k. Fuel for 9,000 mi at about 20 mpg is about $1,400. Private resale in Aug 2027 might be $9.5k-10.5k.
2) 2011 ES 350 at $6.2k (West Allis) or 2009 ES 350 at $7k (Milwaukee): lowest-risk Lexus. Fuel at about 24 mpg is about $1,150. Expected 10-month depreciation is about $800-1,500 if sold privately in August.
3) 2011 Camry V6 with 50k at $13.5k (Cambridge): negotiate toward about $12k. Very low repair risk and strong August resale.
4) 2006 GX 470 at $5.6k (Edgerton): cheapest way into a Lexus 4WD that holds value, but fuel is about $1.9k and the maintenance history is unknown.
Avoid: the 2018 ES at $10.9k (too good to be true), all Land Rovers, the RX 400h (hybrid pack age), and parts cars.

MADISON 捡漏 TACTICS
TIMING
- May graduation dump: UW-Madison spring commencement is mid-May. Departing international (especially Chinese) students must sell before their flights, so late April to early June brings the most motivated private sellers and the deepest discounts. Search results confirm this dynamic: a Chinese-language student car guide says many international students buy through WeChat groups because of the high turnover at graduation, with lower, negotiable prices but no warranty. A smaller second dump comes in mid-December when fall-semester graduates leave.
- Winter slump (Dec-Feb): fewer buyers and dealers trying to hit year-end numbers. RWD cars (IS 250, LS 430/460 RWD, GS) are cheapest in Oct-Jan because local buyers avoid them in snow. Budget $600-900 for winter tires (estimate) if you buy one.
- August move-in: incoming students push demand and asking prices up in late July and August. This hurts buyers but helps this buyer's Aug 2027 exit. List by mid-July on FB Marketplace, 小红书, WeChat groups and the CSSA forum so the car sells before the lease ends.
- Buying in Oct 2026 is roughly neutral: post-August demand has eased, but it is not the bottom. If possible, keep watching until mid-December.

WHERE DEPARTING CHINESE STUDENTS POST CARS
- WeChat groups (UW-Madison CSSA and class-year groups) and 小红书 ("麦迪逊 出车", "Madison 出车", "UW 出车"). 小红书 posts are not indexed by web search, so search inside the app and follow accounts that post "出车" summaries.
- The UWCSSA forum bbs.uwcssa.net (二手买卖 fid=57 and 行@Madison fid=45) has car threads, but the indexed ones are old (2011 Corolla with 77,600 mi; 2001 Camry Solara V6 with 120k at $3,400, marked sold; 2009 Corolla LE with 35k). One thread offers a free Carfax lookup, and another offers help checking used-car VINs. It is now mostly a secondary channel.
- 1point3acres has a 留学生买车 board (forum-124), and huaren.us has buying guides. Neither returned Madison-specific listings.
- Facebook Marketplace and Madison Craigslist are the main English-language private channels. Many departing students cross-post there in May.

PRIVATE VS DEALER PRICE GAP (evidence plus estimates)
- The 2013 RX summary figures put trade-in about $2.5k-3.4k below private party. Dealer retail usually sits above private party, and Madison dealers add a service or doc fee. Estimate: a typical Madison doc fee is a few hundred dollars (not verified in this run).
- Same-site comparison: a private 2012 Camry at $9,800 against a dealer 2012 Camry XLE with 121k at $10,311, which is only about a 5% gap. Private cars are not always cheaper, and small lots post "No Dealer Fee's" ads on Craigslist that look like private sales.
- A Chinese-language guide on huaren.us claims dealer gross margins of 30-40% and at least $3,000 per car. Treat this as a claim, not data. The same source notes that well-kept high-mileage cars are underpriced because US buyers over-weight mileage. That is a real 捡漏 angle for a 10-month hold, where 9,000 more miles changes resale value little.
- Rule of thumb (estimate): expect a real private-party discount of about 10-20% under dealer retail, more for sellers on a deadline such as departing students or people moving.

COMMON MARKETPLACE / 小红书 SCAMS AND RED FLAGS
- Deposit or "shipping" scams: a price far below market (for example the 2018 ES 350 at $10,900), a seller who is "deployed" or "moved away", and a demand for a deposit or full payment by Zelle, wire, gift card or fake "eBay Motors escrow" before you see the car. Never pay before you inspect the car and see the title.
- Title problems: the title is not in the seller's name (a "jumped" or open title, which is typical of curbstoners); a lien on the title with no lien release (common when a student still owes on a car loan, so settle the payoff at the lender); lost titles; and out-of-state salvage, rebuilt or flood titles that were "washed". Run NMVTIS or NICB VINCheck (free) and Carfax or AutoCheck, and compare the VIN on the dash, the door jamb and the title.
- Curbstoning: unlicensed dealers posing as private sellers. Signs include the same phone number on many ads, "No Dealer Fee's" wording, and a seller who cannot show ID matching the title. General knowledge, not verified in this run: Wisconsin requires a dealer license for anyone selling more than a handful of cars (about 5) a year.
- 小红书/WeChat-specific: sellers who have already left the US and use a friend as "代卖" with an unsigned or incorrectly signed title; unpaid parking tickets or tolls; and a car still registered to someone who cannot sign. Insist that the person named on the title signs in front of you, or use a proper power of attorney.
- Odometer fraud: odometer disclosure on the title is required for model-year 2011 and newer. Check the Carfax mileage trail.
- Very cheap Land Rovers or hybrids (the 2007 RR Sport at $1-2k, the RX 400h at $4,250) are usually money pits, not bargains.

HOW A WISCONSIN PRIVATE-SALE TITLE TRANSFER WORKS (general knowledge; not verified by search in this run, so confirm on wisconsindot.gov)
1) The seller completes the seller section of the Wisconsin title: signature(s) of every owner, date, sale price and odometer reading. If a lienholder is listed, the seller must provide a lien release.
2) The license plates stay with the seller in Wisconsin, so the buyer needs their own plates or a temporary plate before driving. WisDOT's online eMV Public service lets a buyer from a private seller apply for title and registration and print a temporary plate.
3) The buyer applies for title and registration promptly (WisDOT sets a short deadline and charges late fees) online or with Form MV1 at a DMV. The buyer pays 5.5% sales tax in Dane County (5% state plus 0.5% county) on the purchase price, the title fee (about $164.50), annual registration (about $85), and the Dane County and City of Madison wheel taxes. Hybrids and EVs pay an extra annual surcharge. Verify every amount on WisDOT's fee calculator.
4) Dane County has no emissions test; only the Milwaukee-area counties require one. Private sellers have no inspection duty. Wisconsin dealers must give a Wisconsin Buyers Guide with a pre-sale inspection disclosure (the Stark listing mentions a completed "Wisconsin Safety Inspection").
5) Buying in Illinois as a WI resident: the IL title is signed over, and you title and pay tax in WI (IL private-party use tax applies to IL residents). The seller keeps the IL plates, so get the WI temporary plate before pickup.
6) When you sell in Aug 2027: sign over the title, keep your plates, and report the sale or transfer to WisDOT (a search result noted that Wisconsin sellers must report a sale within 30 days).
- Always get an independent pre-purchase inspection (estimate: about $100-200 at a Madison shop) and do the handover at a bank so the cashier's check and title change hands together.

AUCTIONS / FLEET / REPO (not searched; the search cap ran out)
- Leads to check manually: Wisconsin Surplus Online (municipal and county fleet auctions), UW-Madison SWAP surplus, City of Madison and Dane County impound or surplus sales, UW Credit Union and Summit CU repo lists, and Enterprise Car Sales Madison. Fleet auctions rarely have Lexus; expect Camry, Prius and Ford/Chevy. They are as-is, often without keys or history, and a poor fit for a first-time US buyer.

FRESHNESS CAVEAT: Craigslist post IDs around 785xxxxxxx line up with a listing the search engine dated May 2025, so many indexed Craigslist ads are more than a year old. Treat every listing above as a lead to re-check live, not as confirmed current inventory.
